title: MANIBELA's 2-day transport strike starts
summary: Transport group Samahang Manibela, Mananakay at Nagkaisang Terminal ng Transportasyon (MANIBELA) on Monday began its two-day transport strike to protest the reported replacement of Land…

blocks.text: Transport group Samahang Manibela, Mananakay at Nagkaisang Terminal ng Transportasyon (MANIBELA) on Monday began its two-day transport strike to protest the reported replacement of Land Transportation Office (LTO) chief Assistant Secretary Markus Lacanilao.
Interviewed on Super Radyo dzBB, MANIBELA national president Mar Valbuena said the group wants Lacanilao to remain in his post to continue the reforms he has implemented at the agency.

“Panglima na ata itong pagpapalit na ito sa hepe ng LTO at sa haba ng panahon, ang haba namin sa kalsada, ngayon lang kami nakaranas ng medyo patas na laban sa pamumuno ni Asec. Markus Lacanilao,” Valbuena said.

(This is probably the fifth time that the LTO chief has been replaced, and in all the time we've been on the road, we've only experienced a fairly fair fight under the leadership of Asec. Markus Lacanilao.)
Valbuena recognized Lacanilao for improving the processing of vehicle registration renewals and driver's licenses, as well as disciplining LTO personnel including those assigned to regional offices.
He claimed that personnel previously removed from the agency over alleged corruption could be reinstated under the planned leadership change.
The reported replacement is Atty. Noreen Bernadette San Luis, according to Valbuena. He said he had heard that President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. had already signed her appointment.
MANIBELA had been discussing the possible leadership change for nearly a month.
Vabuena lamented that transport groups were not consulted or informed about the planned change, despite their concerns.
MANIBELA said the strike could extend to three days depending on the sentiments of the transport sector.
The group planned to march from Agham Road to the LTO headquarters along East Avenue in Quezon City starting at 7 a.m. on Monday, according to a report on GMA News’ Unang Balita.
Meanwhile, the Department of Transportation (DOTr) said there was no official announcement yet from the Office of the President regarding a change in LTO leadership.
The DOTr arranged free rides from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. along several routes:

items: Commonwealth - Cubao (East Avenue and V. Luna)

blocks.text: Also, the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) will offer free rides to assist commuters affected by the strike.

The NCRPO also placed around 6,000 police personnel on alert for the two-day protest, while the Quezon City Police District advised commuters to monitor traffic advisories and report emergencies or incidents requiring police assistance.
